elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon 30 days' prior written notice to MSL"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period
elements.evidence: "MSL shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term
elements.evidence: "MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term"
"upon 30 days' prior written notice" (shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: no early-termination fee mechanic appears; clause provides only "MSL shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any fees prepaid"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term" — no end-of-term Vendor right granted

reasons: All four atomic elements of the preferred position are expressly present in the inserted Section 5.4: Customer convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Vendor (MSL) convenience termination during the initial or any renewal term. Locked target level is achieved.

The fallback is not satisfied (30 days rather than 60–90 days, no early-termination fee, no end-of-term Vendor right), but that is immaterial because the preferred bargain is fully met and the terms are more favourable to us.

Minimality holds: a single concise inserted clause fills a genuine gap (Section 5.0 otherwise permits termination only for cause during the three-year committed term); no untouched sentence was rewritten and no new exception was created.

Intent concern: the insertion uses "Customer", which is not a defined term in this Agreement — the parties are defined as "IBM" and "MSL". As drafted the right and the refund obligation run to an undefined party, creating a dangling mechanic. Replace "Customer" with "IBM" throughout the inserted clause.
